name: cellcell-crossfeed-realistic
description: M7a realistic-diffusivity control for the cross-feeding regime. BYTE-IDENTICAL to cellcell-crossfeed (same localized 20 mM glucose depot in cols 0-18, same secretor/consumer roles and seeds x8-16/x22-30, same acetate_vmax 20 consumer, grow_per_biomass 30) EXCEPT the acetate diffusion coefficient is dropped from the flagship's 15.0 (a 37.5x legibility ratio) to 0.8 -- the PHYSICAL ~2:1 acetate/glucose aqueous ratio (glucose ~600, acetate ~1100 um^2/s). MEASURED OUTCOME (M7a, tests/test_cellcell_m7.py): at the physical ratio the handoff FAILS to complete within a legible horizon. The consumer's own footprint acetate peaks at ~0.21 (vs 1.60 at 37.5x) and its biomass rises only ~2% (1.25 -> ~1.28, vs 1.25 -> 3.79 at 37.5x) before it is competitively displaced off the lattice by the fast-growing secretor around t=20; extending the horizon does not rescue it. The secreted acetate does physically diffuse into the consumer's seed region, but at the physical diffusivity the plume is too slow and too steeply-graded to raise the consumer's own footprint concentration to a feeding level before displacement. Feeding scales monotonically with transport acceleration (consumer biomass gain +14%/+45%/+102%/+203% at 5x/10x/20x/37.5x), so the flagship cross-feed's accelerated transport is load-bearing for the legible handoff at this 6-cell-gap / 20-tick geometry, not cosmetic.

provenance.source: M7a peer-review control -- cellcell-crossfeed re-run at the PHYSICAL acetate/glucose diffusion ratio (0.8 vs 0.4 = 2:1) instead of the flagship's 37.5x legibility ratio
